plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids or values. Since I win only when I have the highest value, and I pay only the second-highest bid, shading my bid down doesn't help—it only risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $49 (the maximum possible), I should bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you only pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks winning at a loss, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $44, bidding exactly $44 ensures I capture positive expected profit whenever the second-highest bid is below my value, without risk of overpaying.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - you never benefit from bidding above or below your value. Bidding higher risks winning and overpaying relative to your value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $22, I should bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.
